lines.text: Welcome aboard. Let's build a company that lasts.
Pick a plot near busy roads. Traffic brings customers through the door.
Every empire starts with one good store. Let's place ours.
Set a price with a healthy margin, but keep an eye on rivals.
Empty shelves earn nothing. Set a restock target so we never run dry.
Press play and let a month run. The books will tell the story.
Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, and cash is king.
Nobody buys what they've never heard of. Let's advertise.
You've got the fundamentals. From here, every decision compounds.
Ground is broken. That capital is committed, so let's make it earn.
That build stretches our cash thin. Make sure it pays back fast.
Construction complete. Staff it, stock it, and put it to work.
The factory is finished. Line up supply so it never sits idle.
Our first sale! Small number, big moment. Now let's make it repeatable.
Record revenue this month. Watch our margins as we scale.
We're selling out. Empty shelves send customers straight to competitors.
Inventory is piling up. That's cash sitting on shelves, not in the bank.
Our cash runway is getting short. Trim costs or line up financing.
We're overdrawn. Every month in the red costs interest and credibility.
lines.tts: We're overdrawn. Every month in the red costs interest, and credibility.

lines.text: Cash is positive again. Nicely done. Let's keep a healthy buffer.
Loan approved. Borrowed money is a tool; make it earn more than it costs.
The bank said no. Strengthen our margins and credit, then ask again.
Loan repaid in full. Less interest, stronger balance sheet.
Our credit rating was downgraded. Borrowing just got more expensive.
Credit rating upgraded. Lenders like what they see.
Interest rates are climbing. Our variable-rate debt just got pricier.
We qualify for a public listing. An IPO could fund real growth.
lines.tts: We qualify for a public listing. An I.P.O. could fund real growth.

lines.text: We're officially public. From now on, every quarter is a report card.
Our share price is surging. The market believes in our story.
Our shares took a beating. Stay calm, and let earnings do the talking.
Dividend declared. Shareholders love a steady, reliable return.
Someone is quietly buying up our shares. Watch for a takeover bid.
A new competitor just entered one of our markets. Expect pressure on price.
We've captured ten percent of this market. That's a real foothold.
A quarter of this market is ours. Competitors will be noticing.
We own half this market now. Defend it with quality and brand.
We're the market leader here. Now the hard part: staying there.
We've lost market leadership here. Time to review price and quality.
It's a price war. Protect our margins; winning at a loss isn't winning.
Research breakthrough! Our technology just moved up a level.
Patent granted. For now, that technology is ours alone.
A rival patented that technology. We'll need a license or a new path.
A recession is here. Conserve cash and protect our core markets.
The economy is recovering. Assets are cheap; a good time to invest.
The economy is booming. Demand is strong, so let's add capacity.
Strong quarter. Revenue and profit are both up. The board is pleased.
A tough quarter. We lost money. Let's find what's dragging us down.
Best quarterly profit yet. That's disciplined execution.
The tax bill is paid. Remember, it's what we keep that counts.
We're edging toward bankruptcy. Raise cash now: borrow, cut costs, or sell assets.
One more month in the red and the creditors take control.
Every objective met. That's a business built to last. Congratulations.
The creditors have taken over. Every great magnate has a second act.
lines.tts: The creditors have taken over. Every great mag-nate has a second act.

lines.text: Time's up. We missed the targets, but the lessons are ours to keep.
We're sitting on idle cash. Money that isn't invested isn't working.
Our brand awareness is fading. A modest ad campaign would help.
Rivals are out-innovating us. Consider building an R&D center.
lines.tts: Rivals are out-innovating us. Consider building an R and D center.

lines.text: One of our factories is idle. Idle capacity is pure overhead.
This city is working well. Consider expanding into another one.
Suppliers are taking a fat margin. Could we make it ourselves?
Good evening. Here's what's moving the markets tonight.
Breaking news: the economy has officially entered a recession.
Economists say the recession is over as hiring picks up nationwide.
Consumer spending hits a record high as the boom rolls on.
The central bank has raised interest rates, effective immediately.
The central bank cuts interest rates to kick-start growth.
Stocks plunge in heavy trading as panic sweeps the exchange.
Stocks close sharply higher in a broad market rally.
Commodity prices spike as supply shortages hit world markets.
Commodity prices tumble on a global supply glut.
A hotly anticipated newcomer debuts on the exchange today.
Another corporate bankruptcy rattles investors this morning.
Scientists unveil a breakthrough that could reshape the industry.
Six million dollars and one city. Let's turn it into a company worth ten.

lines.text: Metropolis: half a million people. The glowing districts are where thirsty customers live.
Construction takes time. Speed things up while the crane works.
Sold against demand: if those numbers ever split, we ran out of stock.
We lost a third of our customers. We can cut price, advertise, or wait.
Borrowing is fine if the new business earns more than the interest.
Same store, new line. More products share the same rent.
Almost there. Keep the shelves full and the brand warm.
Ten million. You've built a real company. Next, we make our own products.

lines.text: We're selling below cost. Every sale loses money.
People are starting to recognise our name.
We're a household name in this city.
Big news. Check how it hits our costs.
We missed a loan payment. The bank is not amused.
Objective complete.
One year left on the clock.
Three months to go. Make them count.
Our first store. Price it smartly and keep those shelves stocked.

lines.text: Every empire starts with a single store. Open Manage, pick a city, and construct your first supermarket.
Shelves do not fill themselves. Assign soft drinks to your store, set your price, and set a restock target.
Time is your engine. Press play and let three months run. Watch the cash begin to flow.
Nobody buys what they have never heard of. Launch a TV campaign and build your brand.
Now scale. Grow your corporate value to $20 million. Your rivals are already moving.
lines.tts: Now scale. Grow your corporate value to twenty million dollars. Your rivals are already moving.
